title: Young Royals
hook: How does Young Royals end? Wilhelm's decision about the throne, the closing of Hillerska, and whether he and Simon finally get to stay together, explained.

sections.heading: Duty against love, one last time
sections.body: The final season puts Wilhelm exactly where the show always promised it would. He is the heir to the Swedish throne, he and Simon have broken up under the strain of palace pressure, and the elite boarding school Hillerska, the place where their relationship began, is facing closure. Everything that made loving Simon impossible is closing in at once. The finale frames the choice as starkly as the series ever has. Wilhelm can keep performing the role he was born into and lose the person he loves, or he can refuse the crown and risk everything else, and he is finally forced to pick.

sections.heading: Wilhelm renounces the throne
sections.body: Wilhelm chooses to walk away from the monarchy. Riding from the now closed Hillerska back toward the palace with his parents, Queen Kristina and Duke Ludvig, he tells them plainly that he is renouncing his place in the line of succession, effectively passing the path to the crown toward his cousin August. Crucially, he insists this is his own decision, made for himself rather than out of rebellion or for Simon's sake. The mother who spent three seasons pressuring him into the role is the one he has to convince, and he does, calmly framing the abdication as inevitable.

sections.heading: The run after Simon
sections.body: Having said the words to his parents, Wilhelm acts on them immediately. He jumps out of the moving royal car and runs after Simon in an unabashed romantic gesture, the show leaning fully into its tender register. The car carrying Simon stops, Simon steps out, and Wilhelm tells him he gave up the throne. The two embrace, kiss and cry, finally free of the institution that kept pulling them apart. After three seasons of secrecy, leaked videos and impossible expectations, the reunion is staged as pure catharsis, the reward the series had been withholding.

sections.heading: Freedom as the thematic payoff
sections.body: The ending argues that the bravest thing Wilhelm can do is choose an ordinary life. The closure of Hillerska, long a symbol of inherited privilege and its cruelty, clears the stage for the central couple to step outside the system entirely. Wilhelm, Simon, Sara and Felice drive away together, leaving behind the constraints that defined them. The payoff is not a fairy-tale coronation but its opposite, a prince trading the crown for the freedom to love openly. The show closes its argument that selfhood matters more than succession, and that Wilhelm finally agrees.

final_image: Wilhelm and Simon, reunited and tearful, drive away from Hillerska alongside Sara and Felice, the camera leaving the school and the monarchy behind as the four head toward an unwritten, freer future.

lingering_questions.q: Does Wilhelm give up the throne in Young Royals?
lingering_questions.a: Yes. In the series finale Wilhelm tells his parents he is renouncing his place in the line of succession, steering the path to the crown toward his cousin August and insisting the choice is his own.

lingering_questions.q: Do Wilhelm and Simon end up together?
lingering_questions.a: They do. After abdicating, Wilhelm runs after Simon's car, tells him he gave up the throne, and the two reunite, kissing and crying before driving away from Hillerska together for a free life.
